findings.title: `handleError`'s new second parameter is used as an exit code by `unhandledRejection` listeners
findings.description: `handleError(err: unknown, exitCode = 1)` is registered directly as a process listener at `packages/cli/src/index.ts:172`: `process.on('unhandledRejection', handleError)`. Node invokes that listener with `(reason, promise)`, so a rejected promise passes its `Promise` object as `exitCode`; `process.exit(exitCode)` at `errors.ts:71` then receives a non-number instead of `1`. The same two-argument callback shape applies to `uncaughtException` (`index.ts:171` passes the origin string). Previously the handler had one parameter, so these listeners worked. Wrap the listeners in single-argument lambdas (e.g. `process.on('unhandledRejection', (err) => handleError(err))`) and add a regression test covering a rejected promise; no test in `packages/cli/tests/utils/errors.test.ts` currently calls the handler with a second argument.

findings.title: `cf validate frontmatter` ignores resolved worktree paths
findings.description: The command destructures only `{ id }` from `resolveProjectWorktree` and always validates `project.projectPath` (`validate.ts:99`), discarding `worktreeId`. Other filesystem commands route to the active worktree: `future.ts:63` uses `resolveOperationPath`, `build.ts:43` uses `resolveProject`, and `guides.ts:39-42` selects `wt.worktreePath`; `applyWorktreeOverlay` in `packages/core/src/utils/worktree-overlay.ts:4-17` replaces `projectPath` with `worktreePath`. Running the gate from a registered worktree therefore validates the main checkout while `process.cwd()`-relative paths at `frontmatterFileValidator.ts:56` are resolved from the worktree, and `--fix` writes against the wrong checkout. The slice design's data flow (`project-documents/user/slices/923-slice.frontmatter-validate-command-dateupdated-stamp.md:127`) says `resolveProjectWorktree (projectPath required)`, so if validating the main root is intentional, it needs to be documented and tested; otherwise use `resolveOperationPath`-style routing and cover it in `packages/cli/tests/commands/validate.test.ts`.

findings.title: `--fix --json` reports original findings with no post-fix state
findings.description: `remaining` is computed at `validate.ts:131` and used for the exit code, but the JSON payload always sets `findings` to the untouched pre-fix array and `errors`/`warnings` to counts derived from it (`validate.ts:139-143`). After a successful `--fix` run, the command exits `0` while `--json` still reports `totalFindings: 1`, `warnings: 1`, and the original finding with its `fixAction`; only `fixed` and `fixLog` reveal success. A scripted consumer must reconstruct post-fix state by cross-referencing `fixLog` and `fixErrors`. The documented shape in `CHANGELOG.md:25` promises counts and `findings[]`, so expose the remaining findings/counts (either as `remaining` fields or by emitting post-fix counts) and add a `--fix --json` test that asserts successful fixes no longer appear as outstanding findings.

findings.title: Test named for a wrong `docType` literal does not exercise that case
findings.description: `it('a wrong docType literal is still caught by the value-constraint logic')` only calls `validateFrontmatter` with two *correct* docTypes (`devlog`, `gate-evidence`, lines 375-385) and an unknown docType (`not-a-real-doctype`, lines 391-394), each asserting zero findings. No case supplies a mismatched literal for a registered schema, so the `docType.values` constraint in `packages/core/src/schema/frontmatterSchema.ts:230-248` is untested for the three newly added schemas — and the comment at lines 389-391 admits unknown types pass through unvalidated. The task plan (`project-documents/user/tasks/923-tasks.frontmatter-validate-command-dateupdated-stamp.md:262-265`) explicitly required a wrong-literal case. Add a test that passes a known schema key with a conflicting `docType` value (e.g. `{ docType: 'devlog', dateCreated: ... }` against `gate-evidence`'s constraint by way of a mismatched literal lookup) and asserts an `Invalid value` finding; also rename this test so it describes the behavior actually verified.

findings.title: Machine-artifact fixes inject a `dateUpdated` field the schema deliberately omits
findings.description: Every `--fix` calls `updateFrontmatterField(..., dateStamp)` unconditionally. That writer (`packages/core/src/introspection/writers/markdownWriter.ts:133-138`) always inserts or rewrites `dateUpdated` unless the fixed field is `dateUpdated` itself. A `review-resolution`, `gate-evidence`, or `devlog` document missing `docType`/`dateCreated` gets an auto-fixable finding; the fix therefore adds `dateUpdated` to an append-only record that `frontmatterSchema.ts:118-123` explicitly says must not require it because the validator has no evidence of an edit. The slice design (`923-slice...md:172`) calls this "convention-correct", but it still contradicts the comment's "append-only records of a moment" framing and the field is not logged in `fixLog`. Either suppress/limit the stamp for these docTypes, or update the schema comment to state that CLI-fixed machine artifacts legitimately carry `dateUpdated`, and add a test pinning the resulting file content.

findings.title: No regression test covers `handleError`'s new exit-code parameter
findings.description: `packages/cli/src/utils/errors.ts:46` gained `exitCode` with the 0/1/2 contract documented in `CHANGELOG.md:25`, but the existing `handleError` suite still only asserts the default `process.exit(1)` (`errors.test.ts:46-47`). The sole coverage of exit `2` is an indirect CLI test (`packages/cli/tests/commands/validate.test.ts:88-96`) that spies on `process.exit` while `handleError` reports the error. Add a direct case asserting `handleError(new UserError(...), 2)` calls `process.exit(2)` and preserves the structured `--json` error body, so the changed contract is pinned at its source.

findings.title: `SEVERITY_ICON`/severity display uses untyped string comparisons
findings.description: `FrontmatterFinding.severity` is the closed union `'warning' | 'error'` (`packages/core/src/schema/frontmatterSchema.ts:28-33`), but this file declares `Record<string, string>` with a `?? '?'` fallback (`validate.ts:15-18`, `62`) and compares `finding.severity === 'error'` with a bare literal (`validate.ts:63`, `140-141`). That permits a misspelled key to silently render `?` and an unhandled severity to be colored as a warning. Prefer a typed `Record<FrontmatterFinding['severity'], string>` plus a shared constant for the severity strings (CLAUDE.md: "Never scatter comparison values across code"), or a small typed helper; this also removes the impossible fallback. The same pattern exists in `check.ts`, but this is new code and need not propagate it.

findings.title: Human output claims "findings" for unfixable items even after a fix attempt
findings.description: `printHumanOutput` prints `Fixed N of findings.length findings` (`validate.ts:78`) and a summary of all original findings (`validate.ts:72`) even when `--fix` was requested for findings that carry no `fixAction` or whose writes failed. The exit code correctly stays `1`, but the label overstates what was attempted. Consider wording like `Fixed N of M fixable findings` and reporting `remaining.length` explicitly; the JSON side has the same ambiguity described above. No action required for correctness.

findings.title: New command wiring, fixtures, and error narrowing verified
findings.description: I read `validate.ts`, `index.ts`, `options.ts`, `errors.ts`, `formatter.ts`, `styles.ts`, `project.ts`, `frontmatterSchema.ts`, `frontmatterFileValidator.ts`, `markdownWriter.ts`, and the associated tests. `registerValidateCommand` is registered at `index.ts:55` and follows the existing shared-option pattern; `resolveProjectWorktree` errors are routed through `handleError(err, 2)` at the process boundary (`validate.ts:178-181`); the fix loop narrows `unknown` catch values with `err instanceof Error` before use (`validate.ts:127-131`) and reports failures rather than swallowing them; and `formatDateProject()` is computed once per run (`validate.ts:108`). The core service parses real files in temp-dir tests (`frontmatterFileValidator.test.ts`), the writer stamp is covered by real-file tests (`markdownWriter.test.ts:66-177`), and the CLI test suite uses Vitest in the centralized `tests/commands/` directory with explicit exit-code assertions. No `any` or hardcoded secrets appear in the changed files. The issues above concern specific behavioral gaps, not the overall structure.
